questions.stem: What is the key difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?

options.text: Prokaryotic cells have a cell wall but eukaryotic cells never do
Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotic cells have one
Eukaryotic cells have DNA but prokaryotic cells do not
Prokaryotic cells are always larger than eukaryotic cells

questions.explanation: The defining feature of prokaryotes (such as bacteria) is that they lack a membrane-bound nucleus. Their DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm in a region called the nucleoid. Eukaryotes have DNA enclosed within a nuclear envelope.
